paper_metadata.title: Thermodynamics guided design and processing of a WC/HEA cermet tool for high temperature friction stir welding

evidence.quote: an integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) approach was applied to design a WC/HEA cermet with high entropy alloy (HEA) binder for better mechanical properties and high temperature performance.
They designed a Co27.4Cr13.8Fe27.4Ni27.4Mo4 (at.%) HEA binder via an integrated computational materials engineering (ICME) approach.

Naval grade ASTM A572 high strength low alloy grade 50 steel (HSLA-50) with 6.35 mm thickness was used as the workpiece material (procured from McMaster-Carr, Elmhurst, IL, USA). The nominal composition of the HSLA-50 material was Fe-0.23C-1.35Mn-0.03P-0.03S-0.4Si (wt.%).

evidence.quote: The WC/HEA powder mixture was mechanically mixed in the planetary ball mill at 200 RPM for 10 hrs. with a ball to powder weight ratio of 20:1 in an ethanol suspension
followed by drying in a convention air oven at 100 °C.

other.heating_cycle: heating to 600 °C, holding 1 min, then ramping to 1200 °C at 100 °C/min and holding at target temperature for 15 min
other.pressure_ramp: ramped up to 50 MPa at 30 MPa/min at beginning and held for entire run
other.tooling: graphite punches and dies, graphite foil 0.15 mm

evidence.quote: The sintering cycle involved heating the powder mixture to 600 °C, holding there for 1 min., then ramping up to a target temperature of 1200 °C at 100 °C/min and holding at target temperature for 15 min., followed by furnace cooling from target temperature to room temperature. The external die pressure was ramped up to 50 MPa at a rate of 30 MPa/min at the beginning of the sintering cycle and held at 50 MPa for the entire run.
Increasing the ball to powder weight ratio and milling time led to the improvement of Cr-rich cluster distribution in the consolidated specimens.
In-depth XRD and TEM analysis of an MA + SPS processed CoCrFeNi HEA indicated the presence of Cr 23 C 6 and Cr 2 O 3 in addition to Cr 7 C 3 in the Cr-rich domains of the microstructure.
